(17 chars); the acip column holds 'THE PRELIMINARIES' — English sitting in the transliteration column — and raw carries the same. The wylie is not Wylie: 'preliminaries' has no legal syllable analysis ('prel' is not a possible stack, 'aries' has no root-letter reading). Three courses carry the IDENTICAL wylie against unrelated English, which proves the string is a repeated editorial running head rather than any segment's text: C01:43 'the preliminaries' / 'I. The Lama and the Word'; C09:171 'the preliminaries' / 'The preliminary division of my text has two parts of its own: the offering of praise, and an identification of that which is to be to be explained.'; C03:303 / 'I. Why the Steps?'. The mechanism is visible where the same header stream was concatenated in front of real Tibetan instead of being stranded alone: C03:298 wylie = "how the teaching was given ,de la 'dir khyab bdag 'khor lo'i mgon po rdo rje 'chang..." and C09:54 wylie = "i. the preliminaries de la 'dir rje btsun chos kyi rgyal po shar tsong kha pa chen po blo...". Sibling header rows of the same class in this course: C03:22 'the asian classics institute'; C03:294 'foreword'; C03:295 'about the authors'; C03:401 'steps shared with those of lesser capacity'; C03:430 'steps shared with those of medium capacity'; C03:476 'open steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:513 'secret steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:558 'the conclusion'. Class boundary, to prevent over-broad remediation: C03:263 wylie='the tshom' / english='Destructive Doubts vi.' IS genuine Wylie (the tshom = doubt) and is NOT part of this class. Effect: the segment carries no Tibetan, so it cannot be aligned, and wylie-side FTS or concordance queries return English strings as though they were Tibetan. No textual correction is possible — the remedy is reclassification as an editorial section header rather than a Tibetan-English parallel segment.

This exceeds the registered heading-only class ("a following section's heading glued onto the end"): the parallel witness P1:77 carries the identical Tibetan and the identical 499-character translation and shows exactly the registered form (translation, then only the next heading "Asian Classics Institute Reading Three: … V. Learning How to Want Freedom"), whereas C03:429 has absorbed a section body. The following heading is separately segmented here as C03:430 ("V. Learning How to Want Freedom"); a spine query for "Three lower realms: According to Buddhism" returns C03:429 and nothing else, so the Reading Nine notes exist in the corpus only as this buried, truncated tail. Alignment impact: the tail inflates English-side counts for this segment (e.g. it is where the ambiguity of common words must be measured) and is unsearchable as notes. The glued endnote bodies are a source-layout defect; the truncation at 'there are five ' is a pipeline defect. Siblings C03:376 and C03:620 (the Reading Eight and Ten note blocks) are also glued and also exactly 1500 characters; see the class entry filed alongside for the corpus-wide count. class_references.evidence: Found by the skeptic pass on C03:429 (E-106), which asked why that field ends mid-sentence at 'there are five ' and measured length(english) = 1500 exactly. Census 2026-09-01 on build/hgm_spine_v27_2.db: 186 segments have length(english) = 1500 (DDA 28, C18 15, C12 14, C13 12, C11 11, Sunlight 11, C17 10, C03 9 - including C03:376, 429, 620, the Reading Eight/Nine/Ten note blocks - MB2 8, C16 7, and 25 further courses); 34 segments EXCEED 1,500, so at least one ingest path does not apply the cap and its reach is not uniform. What is lost is not always apparatus: wherever the cap falls inside a translation, the corpus has no English for the rest of the Tibetan and nothing can align it. The 186 are a floor for the affected rows (a row cut at exactly the cap is certain; a row that happened to be shorter is unaffected).
